text.text_excerpt: Oh my. This was the location of my niece's wedding on Saturday night and we had the whole space and it was GORGEOUS! All the out of town guests were super impressed with the historic FQ charm and I was really impressed with the staff and the food. All the items from the fancy crudite display to the passed appetizers to the crawfish ettouffe to the amazing mashed potatoes were yummy. The staff was really accommodating to the various needs of my family, from finding an additional chair for older parents to pretending I wasn't sitting in a corner on the floor with a child crashed in my lap. My best friend growing up had her wedding reception here this past weekend. It was a beautiful setting, as almost any historic building in the French Quarter is, but the real star of the night was the food. Latrobe's catering created a fabulous menu. Roast beef, mashed potatoes, glazed carrots, crawfish penne pasta, shrimp & grits, crawfish beignets, boudin balls, raw oysters, boiled shrimp, artichoke cheesecake -- everything was amazing. Their shrimp & grits puts everybody else's to shame. Also, the Pimm's Cup was a refreshing change from wine & "heavier" cocktails. Amazing food + beautiful setting = wedding reception perfection.

What a cool spot for a wedding! The food was amazing - seafood gumbo was the best I've ever had. It had huge chunks of seafood in it, no skimping there. And the seafood tortellini and oyster bar were also great. Beautiful inside. Vaulted ceilings, historic charm and beauty. My only complaint was the three rooms. Because of the size of the wedding I attended, there were people in all three at all times and food was being served in all of them. It was a bit challenging to navigate, and I missed two entire food stations! But for a smaller wedding that starts in one room and then moves into the other, this would be perfect.
